problem: GUIDER, the authors' prior probabilistic framework for navigation and manipulation intent inference, only predicts intent, and the operator still has to command the robot manually. It also has no semantic or language context to narrow the candidate objects and areas.
motivation: Robots that collaborate with people must infer intent quickly and then act on it, or they add cognitive load and conflict with the user. Open-vocabulary VLMs/LLMs can supply mission context, but earlier work has not fused it as an explicit probability factor with continuous intent beliefs, nor closed the loop from inference to assistance.
key_idea: Use a zero-shot VLM (scoring object crops against a mission prompt) plus an optional text-only LLM (ranking detected labels) as a semantic prior that weights GUIDER's navigation and manipulation beliefs, and trigger shared-autonomy or autonomous assistance once the fused belief passes a threshold.
insight: This is a proposal with no experiments, so nothing is empirically shown. The claim is that a prompt-conditioned semantic prior suppresses irrelevant objects and areas, which shrinks the search space and makes intent inference more transparent. It also lets the operator change the mission prompt at any time and have the weights update immediately.
method: Vision module: YOLOv8 detects objects and SAM segments instances, giving a class label and an image crop for each object.
VLM relevance scoring: a pre-trained VLM takes a crop and the mission prompt and returns the likelihood that the object matches the goal.
LLM ranking: a text-only LLM is given the list of detected labels and ranks their relevance to the mission.
Semantic prior fusion: the scores are normalised and multiplied into GUIDER's evolving navigation and manipulation likelihoods, and objects with very low combined scores are pruned.

Commitment rule: when the fused belief exceeds a confidence threshold, the system invokes a shared-autonomy controller (control axes reconfigured toward the goal) or an autonomous mode (base navigates and arm grasps).
Dynamic prompts: the operator can edit the mission prompt at any time (specific, categorical or relational) and the beliefs update immediately.

setting.backbone: Pre-trained VLM and text-only LLM (unspecified, frozen, zero-shot) + YOLOv8 + SAM, fused into GUIDER's probabilistic belief model
setting.observation: Onboard RGB camera on a mobile manipulator, plus operator controller input, an occupancy map and a synergy map (from GUIDER)
setting.action_space: Mobile-base navigation to the selected area or object, plus arm grasp; shared-autonomy control-axis reconfiguration
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (planned; living-room scene with Franka Panda arm on Clearpath Ridgeback base)

numbers_note: Extended abstract with a planned study only; no results are reported.
results: No experimental results are reported. The planned evaluation compares against original GUIDER with assistance added, using time to confident prediction, intent accuracy and assistance completion time.
limitations: No implementation results or evaluation yet; the study is only planned.
Simulation only for now; robustness to real-world lighting and occlusion is untested.
The specific VLM/LLM, the threshold values and the fusion details are not specified.
